questions.prompt: A page is at https://www.contoso.com/courses/index.html and has no base element. For each statement about path-relative and absolute URLs, select Yes or No. Here, path-relative excludes network-path references beginning with //.

pairs.left: A path-relative link must include a protocol and server name.
lessons/intro.html can reference a document in a subdirectory of the current page’s directory.
images/logo.png can reference an image on a different server without changing the document base URL.

questions.explanation: With no base element, a path-relative URL is resolved against the current document URL and keeps its server. images/logo.png cannot name another server. A network-path reference beginning //host is a different form and is outside this explicitly scoped question.

questions.prompt: Complete the link pseudo-class rules: unvisited links red, visited links blue, links under the pointer orange, and links during activation green. Each selector may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
questions.explanation: Use a:link for unvisited links, a:visited for visited links, a:hover for pointer hover, and a:active for activation. Keeping these equal-specificity rules in link, visited, hover, active order lets the interactive states override earlier colors.

questions.prompt: For each statement about CSS, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

pairs.left: A CSS comment starts with /* and ends with */.
The em unit always refers to the root element’s font size.
width: 50% always means half the viewport width.
A font-family fallback list can help when the preferred font is unavailable.

questions.explanation: CSS comments use /* ... */. em does not always refer to the root font size; rem does. Percentage references depend on the property and context, so width: 50% is not always half the viewport. A font-family fallback list helps when the preferred font is unavailable. These statements replace ambiguous source generalizations.

questions.prompt: Complete this Blue Yonder Airlines page: load style.css as a stylesheet, load _js/form.js as an external script, set the page title, and show the specified fallback when scripting is disabled. Select the element name for each blank.
questions.exhibit:
<head>
  <[1] rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  <[2] src="_js/form.js"></[2]>
  <[3]>Blue Yonder Airlines</[3]>
</head>
<body>
  <[4]>Your browser does not support JavaScript!</[4]>
</body>
questions.explanation: link with rel="stylesheet" loads the CSS file; script with src loads JavaScript; title names the browser tab; noscript supplies fallback content when scripting is disabled. meta cannot link a stylesheet. Missing source choices and targets have been replaced with a complete adapted exercise.

questions.prompt: Evaluate the term Static positioning in this statement: “Static positioning removes an element from normal flow and uses top/right/bottom/left offsets relative to its nearest positioned ancestor’s containing block.” Assume such an ancestor exists and no transform establishes another containing block. Choose the replacement term, or No change is needed.
questions.explanation: Absolute positioning removes the element from normal flow. In this stated setup, offsets are measured from its nearest positioned ancestor’s containing block. Relative positioning instead offsets an element from its normal position and preserves its flow space. The source’s vague wording and Relative key have been corrected.
